newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner pleased to keep Aaa rating.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner pleased to keep Aaa rating.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG said on Friday that it was pleased that the latest report by Moody's Investors Service retained the Aaa rating on the bank's unsecured debt.
"We are pleased that the rating has been maintained," a spokeswoman told Reuters.

Moody's said on Friday it was leaving unchanged the Aaa rating on Dresdner but has given the bank negative long-term and financial strength ratings. The spokeswoman played down the significance of the latter, saying that the main factor was that the unsecured debt rating was not in danger.
The news on Dresdner Bank came only two days after Moody's said it had put rival Deutsche Bank's Aaa long-term debt rating and A financial strength rating under review for a possible downgrade.

Equities traders said the news on Deutsche Bank weighed on all financial sector shares, with the news on Dresdner adding further pressure. Dresdner shares fell 20 pfennigs to 40.45 markst in floor trading on Friday.
Moody's said the existing rating was based on Dresdner's "superior creditworthiness".
"We continue to view Dresdner as a very strong and financially stable banking group both by German and international standards," Moody's said in a statement.
But it added, "The outlook for the long-term and financial strength ratings are negative."
